name: Teleprompter and captions
intro: Where the scroll follows your voice and the captions are accurate, and where the script freezes and the export slaps on a watermark.

apps.title: Teleprompter
apps.verdict: People praise the simplicity, smooth scrolling, remote control, and generous free version that makes them buy the lifetime license to support the developers. The weak spots are concrete: no voice-synced scrolling, mirrored text and remote control moved to the paid tier, and recorded video can come out washed out and lower quality than the native camera.
apps.loved: Simplicity, smooth scrolling, remote control, generous free version, clean audio with noise reduction, sharing to social media
apps.weak: No voice-driven scrolling, mirrored text and remote locked behind pay, recording quality worse than native camera, crashes during recording, recorded clips disappear
apps.whoFor: Bloggers and YouTube creators who want a reliable teleprompter with smooth scrolling and a remote and don't mind paying once

quotes.text: The auto scroll is suppose to move as you speak....sure does...if music plays (with no one is singing), when other people speak in the background
The fatal flaw is the inability to save a desired scroll speed. Every time you open a script it reverts back to the default 50, which is way too fast.
the Scroll up and down functions on a presentation remote (like podcaster) no longer works with this app. So I bit the bullet and got another teleprompter app for $90/year.
So many times after recording a several minute video, I click the camera to save it, and my recording disappears. That’s very frustrating.

apps.title: Video Teleprompter Lite
apps.verdict: People value it above all for being free and quick to learn: read your text looking into the camera and record a clip without stumbling. The main pain is saving and exporting: short clips go through fine, but long ones won't save, the app spins forever, the phone overheats, plus the watermark and the on-screen text that gives away you're reading are annoying.
apps.loved: Completely free, quick to learn, helps you read without stumbling and not look robotic, reliable on short clips
apps.weak: Long clips won't save and hang in endless loading, phone overheats on export, watermark stays even after paying, large text under the lens gives away reading, portrait-only recording
apps.whoFor: Beginners and anyone shooting short talking-head clips who doesn't want to pay for a teleprompter

quotes.text: It records in profile only, and it’s obvious you’re reading in the video because this text is so large below the lens. Not useful for me.
I record for YT and need the background blurred but you can’t adjust the f stop after you record the video nor can you do cinematic mode.
I hate how each time I scroll back on the teleprompter, it pauses the video, then you have the end the video and delete the old video and redo it all.
I recorded a long video using this app and it would not let me export at the end!!! My phone just got extremely hot... and the app showed that it was fully done exporting.

apps.title: AI Captions for Videos: VidCap
apps.verdict: The main value is speed: subtitles for a long video, even an hour long, are ready in minutes, and for people like those making medical education clips that saves real time. Accuracy is decent in English but drops on quiet and non-English speech, and local transcription on Mac stalls. The sore spot that costs it five-stars is export: some people found the captions vanished from the finished file on playback.
apps.loved: Fast subtitles even for hour-long videos, good English accuracy, simple clear preview, handy subtitle splitting
apps.weak: Captions disappear from the exported file, slow and stalling local transcription on Mac, weak on quiet and non-English speech, can't add custom fonts, pricey for a thin feature set
apps.whoFor: People who regularly caption long videos for study or work and value speed over fine-grained control.

quotes.text: It gave me the closed caption for my video. Took less than eight seconds.

apps.title: Teleprompter.com
apps.verdict: The main thing people love is that auto-scroll follows their speaking pace and they look into the camera instead of darting their eyes. But the price stings, support was replaced by a bot that never answers on point, and mirrored text is locked behind pay, so you can't use it free with a real teleprompter rig. Plus complaints about 30 fps instead of 60 and charges after cancelling.
apps.loved: Auto-scroll matching speaking pace, looking straight into the camera, simplicity even for older users, working across cameras and devices, adjustable text width
apps.weak: High price, bot-only support with no answers, mirrored text locked behind pay, only 30 fps instead of 60, auto-scroll drops out during recording, charges after cancelling
apps.whoFor: Creators and podcasters who care about scrolling at their own speaking pace and looking into the camera, if they're willing to pay a subscription

quotes.text: Finally, I’m not looking “over there” to read my script, then “over here”to look in the camera. And the “auto-scroll” follows MY pace.

apps.title: Telepromptr
apps.verdict: Experienced presenters and shooters value it for the core of a teleprompter: editing the script on the fly, adjusting speed and font size, text right above the lens for eye contact, working with both a formal teleprompter and a tablet on a stand. But the details spoil it: script import is very clunky, renaming scripts scrambles names and texts, and the promised Bluetooth keyboard hasn't worked for many for years. It also has no built-in video recording, you need a second app.
apps.loved: Editing the script on the fly, speed and font-size control, text above the lens for eye contact, works with a formal teleprompter and a tablet on a stand, 4k recording
apps.weak: Clunky script import, renaming scrambles names and texts, Bluetooth keyboard broken for years, no built-in recording so you need a second app, awkward speed steps
apps.whoFor: Presenters, hosts and people shooting talking-head video who need a reliable teleprompter with on-the-fly editing, if clunky script import isn't a dealbreaker.

quotes.text: the speed I really need 95% of the time is somewhere between speed 12 and speed 13. Just about every time, speed 12 is too slow for my talent, and speed 13 is too fast.
You can now pause which is especially helpful for me because I do sometimes go off script.

apps.title: Teleprompter Pro
apps.verdict: People love it for smooth scrolling and remote control, and they pull it into all kinds of scenarios from recording video to song lyrics at live concerts. But some hit breakage after updates: syncing between devices jumps and drops out with hours of work lost, uploaded songs disappear from folders, and the set speed isn't remembered. Importing multiple scripts and arranging them into folders is clumsy.
apps.loved: Smooth scrolling, best external remote control, works for voiceover and song lyrics, Bluetooth foot-pedal integration, intuitive on a shoot
apps.weak: Sync between devices breaks with lost work, uploaded songs disappear, set speed not remembered, clumsy import and folder arrangement of scripts, glitches after updates
apps.whoFor: People who work a lot from a remote: video creators, musicians with song lyrics on stage, and prompter operators on shoots

quotes.text: when you tap the turtle icon or whatever to set the speed it doesn’t remember it. so when i come back and when to perform the script at the same speed i had last time i can’t figure out what it was!

my podcaster presentation remotes (I have 2) don’t allow the screen to scroll up or down when I press the button on the remote. I tried it on 2 separate iPhones and doesn’t work. It took 2 1/2 hours of my time trying to troubleshoot.

apps.title: Teleprompter For Video -FoxCue
apps.verdict: People use it to learn lines and film talking-head clips: students submit video assignments, creators record short updates, the audio is clean, and it's easy to learn. It stumbles on recording and money: for some an error pops up when uploading a finished clip, video downloads cropped, a FoxCue logo lands in the intro, and downloading your own clip is locked behind a subscription.
apps.loved: Helps learn lines fast, simple talking-head recording, clean audio, handy for school video assignments and work updates, lots of styling options
apps.weak: Error when uploading a finished clip, video downloads cropped without the full frame, FoxCue logo in the intro, downloading your own clip locked behind a subscription, crashes and a nagging rate prompt between takes
apps.whoFor: Students and creators who need to learn lines and film a tidy talking-head clip for school or social

apps.title: Zeemo: AI Video&Auto Captions
apps.verdict: Fast at making captions and especially strong with bilingual subtitles, export is quick. Breaks on auto-captions for some (glitches, cuts off), no video cropping, weak Arabic support and clunky text editing. Watermark and paywall annoy those expecting free.
apps.loved: Fast export, bilingual subtitles, simple caption overlay, decent recognition accuracy
apps.weak: Auto-captions sometimes glitch and cut off, cannot crop or zoom video, weak Arabic support, awkward text editing, watermark on free version
apps.whoFor: People editing short social clips who need bilingual subtitles

quotes.text: I tried to translate a 10 second clip of someone singing that was in Russian and for that whole clip it said “translation by dima”.

apps.title: Auto Caption Video Subtitles
apps.verdict: A simple, fast way to add subtitles, and many value the accuracy and the wide choice of styles, with some paying for it for years. It breaks on longer clips (crashes), sometimes exports video with no sound, and mixes up languages in the captions. People also bristle that the 'free' label is conditional and the weekly price feels steep.
apps.loved: Recognition accuracy, lots of caption styles and color combos, simple and fast, saves time
apps.weak: Crashes on long videos, sometimes exports with no sound, captions come out in a mix of wrong languages, weekly subscription feels expensive
apps.whoFor: People cranking out short social clips who want to slap subtitles on quickly

apps.title: Teleprompter－Read script
apps.verdict: A simple free teleprompter that genuinely helps you keep your pace and stop rambling on camera, and that is what people value it for. But users complain the text freezes or flies by too fast with no real speed control, and the script often can't be saved so you have to paste it in again. On top of that the screen sometimes goes black or white during recording and audio starts out too quiet.
apps.loved: Free, simple, helps keep pace and stop rambling, easy to read the script while filming
apps.weak: Text freezes during recording, scroll too fast with no proper speed control, can't save the script, screen goes dark or white while filming, quiet audio at the start, no pauses in the script
apps.whoFor: Beginners at short-form video who want a free teleprompter to read text to camera without losing their place

quotes.text: as soon as you start recording the text starts scrolling with no way to stop it… it’s not fun usi

apps.title: Video Teleprompter
apps.verdict: People praise it for the teleprompter, script sync across devices, and speed control from a Bluetooth remote, and they use it even for weekly church filming. The weak spots are concrete: the advertised green screen doesn't work right for many, it crops and zooms the background oddly, audio desyncs with external mics like DJI, and there's no voice scrolling or 60 fps recording. Plus a confusing multi-app setup with add-on purchases.
apps.loved: Teleprompter for filming, script sync across devices, speed control from a Bluetooth remote, simplicity paired with a mic and remote, good camera
apps.weak: Green screen doesn't work as promised, odd background cropping and zoom, audio desync with external mics, no voice scrolling or 60 fps, confusing add-on purchases
apps.whoFor: People who regularly film talking-head clips with a remote and external mic, for example for church or a YouTube channel

quotes.text: I love all of the teleprompter apps from this company, and I absolutely love that I can sync scripts across my computer, iPad and phone.

apps.title: Teleprompter for Video Pro
apps.verdict: A powerful teleprompter with video recording, AI audio cleanup and subtitles, and the prompter can be moved under the camera, which many like. The main shared anger is about money: you're only warned about payment when you go to download the video after an hour of recording, and the footage just gets stuck inside. On the technical side, recording crashes around the thirty-second mark, voice scroll reacts to any noise rather than speech, and recorded takes sometimes vanish.
apps.loved: Prompter moves under the camera, AI audio and background cleanup, accurate subtitles, speed control, lots of post-processing tools
apps.weak: You only learn about payment at download after an hour of recording, recording crashes around thirty seconds, voice scroll reacts to noise not speech, recorded takes disappear, expensive monthly price
apps.whoFor: People who regularly shoot talking videos from a script and want a prompter with recording and audio cleanup

quotes.text: I don't understand why you have to record with the camera. In my case, I may only need my voice.

apps.title: MixCaptions: Video Captions
apps.verdict: People grab it to slap captions on social videos fast, and for that core job it delivers: auto-transcription around 80% accurate, flexible text, fonts, colors, and any aspect ratio. It breaks on speed and reliability: for some it stalls 10-30 minutes on a one-minute clip or fails entirely, and the watermark sometimes won't lift even after paying.
apps.loved: Fast speech auto-transcription, simple interface, font and color control, free text placement, multiple aspect ratios, Chinese caption support
apps.weak: Transcription sometimes drags 10-30 minutes or freezes, watermark stays after paying, auto-captions mishear some words, feels like a rushed macOS port
apps.whoFor: People cranking out short social clips who want captions on fast without deep editing

quotes.text: customizable text, fonts, colors, shadows, etc • can place text anywhere on video • various video aspect ratios to choose from
I just joined RedNote and needed an app that could add Chinese captions on my videos. This one was super easy to use.
empresarial para traducir videos de 30 min y nada no los traduce solamente crea los subtitulos pero no lo traduce al idioma que eliges

apps.title: Teleprompter App Record Videos
apps.verdict: People grab it to record a talking-head video from a script without needing a second device to read from, and non-techy folks find it genuinely easy: '1, 2, 3, video done'. It breaks elsewhere: it only saves the first take, forcing you to rewrite the script and re-record, and after you pay it crashes when exporting a video with captions. The nonstop review-nag popping up mid-recording is a real annoyance.
apps.loved: Recording from a script without a second device, easy for non-techy people, fast result
apps.weak: Only the first take saves and you have to rewrite the script, crashes when exporting video with captions, ads even for paying users, no scroll-speed control, review-nag pops up mid-recording
apps.whoFor: People shooting short talking-head videos from a script who don't want to fuss with tech or a second device.

apps.title: Veme.ly: Video Subtitles
apps.verdict: The auto-captions really are handy and simple, you can move the video and text layers around the canvas, and support responds fast and fixes issues, which is what people value. But on longer clips the export drags and crashes before finishing, finished subtitles sometimes vanish after saving, and the output resolution is worse than the preview. People are also annoyed that a subscription is forced for the most basic thing, adding subtitles.
apps.loved: Simple accurate auto-captions, you can move video and text layers around the canvas, responsive fast support, handy for short social clips
apps.weak: Export crashes on long videos, subtitles disappear after saving, output resolution worse than the preview, subscription forced for basic subtitles, lip-sync lag, updates remove features
apps.whoFor: People making short social clips who want simple auto-subtitles with control over where the text sits in the frame

quotes.text: the subtitles disappear after i wait the two minutes it takes to export. i’ve tried multiple times.

apps.title: Teleprompter for Video
apps.verdict: The app genuinely makes it easier to film and read a script as you record, which people thank it for after a year of use. But there's a lot of pain around the trial: people get charged instantly instead of after three days, with no warning. Plus recording is locked inside the app with no export to TikTok or Instagram, the size reaches 8 gigabytes, and recording errors pop up on newer iPhones.
apps.loved: Easy reading of the script while recording, time saved without memorizing, help for beginners filming, reasonable extra charge for needed features
apps.weak: Charged instantly instead of a three-day trial, recording locked inside the app with no export to social apps, size up to 8 gigabytes, recording errors on newer iPhones, needs internet to save a script
apps.whoFor: Beginners and hobbyists who need a simple teleprompter for filming video with the script read right on screen

quotes.text: It forces you to stay in the app to record. It won’t let you use it with TikTok, IG, or any other platform beyond its own! Waste of money!
The pop-up teleprompter does not show text when the native camera is open. Nor does the popup start when you zoom out with your fingers.

apps.title: Auto Captions: Video Subtitles
apps.verdict: When the auto-captions fire they generate nicely and content folks like it, and the layout itself is simple. But reliability lets it down: it often captions only the first third of a video and then stops, manual fixing is clunky, and export drops the frame rate and degrades picture quality. Text-size and color issues plus constant asset re-downloading that crashes the app are also annoying.
apps.loved: Solid auto-caption generation when it works, simple layout, helps make content, sometimes no signup and free
apps.weak: Captions only part of the video and cuts off, frame-rate drop and quality loss on export, clunky manual editing, can't change text size or aspect ratio, crashes during endless asset downloads
apps.whoFor: People making short social clips who want fast auto-captions and can tolerate rough edges on longer videos.

apps.title: AutoCap: Auto Video Captions
apps.verdict: It used to be one of the best auto-caption apps: solid AI recognition, easy editing, works in many languages including Arabic. But recent updates broke a lot: video sound disappears while editing, they added an awkward zoom that makes captions impossible to drag, and crashes mid-work got more frequent. Recognition accuracy also stumbles, so you spend a lot of time fixing captions by hand.
apps.loved: Good AI recognition and word highlighting, easy caption editing, works in many languages, was convenient before the updates
apps.weak: New updates broke the interface, captions impossible to move because of the zoom, video sound disappears during editing, crashes mid-work, inaccurate recognition needs manual fixing
apps.whoFor: People making vertical clips with captions in various languages who can live with the fallout from updates

quotes.text: the caption is not accurate so you spend a ton of time editing your captions. If it were not for the time spent editing the auto cap, I would easily give it a five!
I'm surprised there's no option for the 9:16 ratio, crucial for many streaming platforms.

apps.title: PromptSmart Lite Teleprompter
apps.verdict: The core value is one thing: a free version to try voice scrolling, and in quiet it works like magic, which has come through on important speeches like a eulogy at a funeral. But the free version is too restricted: recording only three minutes, often no recording without paying, and just one script, so you can't tell if the $30 paid version will suit you. Plus crashes when rotating the screen and voice recognition failures in noise and with an accent.
apps.loved: Free trial of voice scrolling, keeps pace with speech even with echo, comes through on important speeches, in-app editing, connecting cloud drives
apps.weak: Recording only three minutes, often no recording without paying, only one script, crashes when rotating the screen, recognition failures in noise and with an accent
apps.whoFor: People who want to try voice scrolling ahead of buying the paid version, especially for an important speech in a quiet setting

quotes.text: I was amazed at how well the app was able to keep up with my voice despite the significant echo in the large church sanctuary.
It worked for the first two sessions, but then it seems to choke quite a bit with long transcripts.

apps.title: VDIT - Video Caption Editor
apps.verdict: People praise the simple, handy editor for captions and text over video. But the main pain is lost work: the app deletes projects after saving, wipes material if you remove the source files from storage, and freezes and crashes on export. It also annoys people that after updates the best features like custom music, sounds, and no watermark moved behind pay.
apps.loved: Simple handy editor, text and captions over video, easy start for beginners, was good for memes and fun edits
apps.weak: Deletes projects after saving, wipes material when source files are removed, crashes and freezes on export, custom music and sounds moved behind pay, slowdowns after an update
apps.whoFor: People making short clips with captions and text over video who want a simple editor on hand

apps.title: Captions for Videos - SubMe AI
apps.verdict: Those who get lucky like it for simply overlaying subtitles without the fuss that plagues other apps. But reliability is weak: videos won't load on the first try or at all, export freezes at exactly 90 percent, and the sound sometimes disappears. Plus a big ugly watermark across the frame, no way to fix typos in names, and, per reviews, an insanely hiked price billing by the second.
apps.loved: Simple subtitle overlay without fuss, easy subtitle formatting, accurate subtitles when it works
apps.weak: Videos won't load first time or at all, export freezes at 90 percent, sound disappears, big watermark across the frame, can't edit the text, hiked price billed by the second
apps.whoFor: People who want to quickly overlay subtitles on a short video and can tolerate a watermark and loading glitches.

apps.title: Verba: Auto Captions for Video
apps.verdict: It recognizes captions noticeably more accurately than rivals, catching your words even with noise and a second speaker far off, and that's what gets praised. But exporting the finished clip drags on for 40 minutes, stalls at 70 percent, and locks up the phone while it runs. The subscription also grates: you can't customize captions or download the video without a yearly payment, and after buying premium people run into a daily limit.
apps.loved: Accurate speech recognition even with noise and a distant second voice, beautiful subtitle designs, translation, a simple fast interface
apps.weak: Export takes 40 minutes and stalls near the end, freezes the phone, Arabic text comes out reversed, caption customization and downloads only on a yearly subscription, daily limit after paying for premium
apps.whoFor: People who care about accurate auto-captions and pretty subtitle design and can put up with slow exports and a yearly subscription

apps.title: Video Resizer Subtitles Maker
apps.verdict: The core job it does cleanly: resizes video, adds background, borders and colors, transcribes speech and burns captions right into the clip, and the flow is fast and clear. It stumbles on quality and stability: exports often squash the picture to 270-480p, adding blurred background or captions freezes or crashes the app, and a huge watermark covers the whole frame.
apps.loved: Fast video resizing, adding background, borders and colors, auto-captions burned into the clip, clean no-frills flow
apps.weak: Exports drop quality to 270-480p, freezes and crashes when adding captions and blurred background, huge full-frame watermark, can't reopen past projects, cap on clip length
apps.whoFor: People quickly fitting clips to social sizing and adding captions without heavy editing

apps.title: PromptSmart Pro - Teleprompter
apps.verdict: People buy this app for one thing: scrolling follows your voice, pausing when you pause, and it feels like magic compared to plain teleprompters. But lately it's gotten glitchy: voice scrolling regularly stalls or lags, text and camera load slowly, and the screen freezes and won't save video. It also annoys people with a subscription price for what used to be a one-time buy, and it works noticeably worse on Android than on iPad.
apps.loved: Scrolling follows your voice with pauses, saves a solo creator's nerves, works great in quiet, reliable on iPad, pairs with a teleprompter rig
apps.weak: Voice scrolling stalls and lags, slow loading of text and camera, freezes without saving video, expensive subscription instead of a one-time buy, weak on Android
apps.whoFor: Solo creators and speakers who care about voice-driven scrolling without setting a speed, especially on iPad and in a quiet setting

quotes.text: The app simply works. Having the voice recognition cue is a night and day difference to “dumb” teleprompter apps.
was on a professional job and the voice scroll option did not work. We switched to the remote and it was super buggy.

apps.title: Teleprompter App
apps.verdict: When it works, the teleprompter genuinely helps you read the script, keep your pace, and not break eye contact with the camera, which is why creators praise it. But money is charged before a person even downloads the app, you can't film a single clip for free, and filming itself gets stuck in landscape even after paying. People also complain that good takes get lost while the bad ones are the ones that save.
apps.loved: Smooth script scrolling, adjustable speed and text size, helps keep pace and eyes on camera, built-in recording, all in one place
apps.weak: Charged before downloading, can't film a single clip for free, stuck in landscape even after paying, loses good takes and saves the bad ones
apps.whoFor: Short-form video and lecture creators who want a teleprompter with recording all in one place, but only if ready for an aggressive subscription and billing risks

quotes.text: The built-in recorder is a big plus.
Every bad take, it saves, every video I complete that I’m prepared to use is magically lost. Do not download this app.

apps.title: Captions: AI Edits Your Video
apps.verdict: People praise how easy it is and how it saves editing time on short phone clips. It breaks down on money and AI quality. Many complain you have to pay just to save and export your video, the AI edits look obvious and get no views, and a recent update broke moving text.
apps.loved: Fast editing of short videos from the phone, time saved, simple start for beginners, handy fonts and captions
apps.weak: Paying to save and export the clip, obvious AI edits with no payoff, update broke dragging text, random credit grants, sign-in trouble
apps.whoFor: Beginners shooting short vertical clips on a phone who want quick captions without hassle

apps.title: Teleprompter: Floating Notes
apps.verdict: The strong feature is a floating script window over the front camera and easy tuning of text color and size, which people praise. It breaks on stability and ads: on the free version ads pile in so you can't even test it, the floating window changes its own size and speed, and the app freezes and loses recordings and even saved scripts after paying.
apps.loved: Floating script window over the front camera, fine control of text color and size, works with the native cinematic camera, beautiful execution, one-time lifetime purchase
apps.weak: Ads on the free version block real testing, floating window changes its own size and speed, freezes losing recordings and scripts after paying, pop-ups pushing third-party cleaners, awkward start and stop
apps.whoFor: People filming themselves on the front camera who want to hold eye contact with a floating prompter

quotes.text: I love the floating ability over the front facing camera but I can’t h
the floating screen is unstable and not reliable. It would change size, shape, speed, all on its own, despite me setting the settings.
Wanted to use the native iPhone Cinematic Camera in selfie mode and this app gets it done.

apps.title: MixBit: Subtitles for Videos
apps.verdict: Auto-captions that genuinely help some people and are easy to edit, with translation and a nice simple interface. But there's a lot of money pain: people get charged for a yearly subscription even after canceling the same day, and you can't save or send a video without paying. The core is shaky too: recognition often misses, skips long phrases, text is either late or jumps out early, and the watermark can't be removed for free.
apps.loved: Auto-captions save time, easy to fix wrong words, translation works, simple clear interface
apps.weak: Charged for a yearly subscription even after canceling the same day, can't save or send video without paying, recognition misses and skips phrases, text lagging or premature, can't remove the watermark for free
apps.whoFor: People who need to quickly slap auto-captions on a short video and don't mind wrestling with payment

apps.title: BIGVU Teleprompter Captions AI
apps.verdict: People value the teleprompter for recording clips and the fast support that actually replies. But it glitches often: scroll speed jumps by itself, the camera opens as a black screen, and it stops working after an iPhone update. There are also complaints about being charged after cancelling and free videos getting cut off at nine minutes.
apps.loved: Teleprompter for recording content, fast live support, one-on-one instruction calls, professional-looking results
apps.weak: Scroll speed jumps on its own, up-down buttons do nothing, black screen instead of camera, crashes, incompatibility with the new iPhone, charges after cancelling
apps.whoFor: People recording talking-head clips who want a teleprompter with human support on hand

quotes.text: I swear the prompt speed changes by itself, pressing the up and down buttons do nothing and it will mess you up while reading.

When trying to record videos and start at a new point within the script, the script jumps way far ahead and you can’t back up. It takes me hours to record a five minute script because I keep having to start over.

apps.title: Subcap: Captions AI, Subtitles
apps.verdict: People pick it for auto-captions on longer clips, and the speech recognition gets praised even with noisy audio. The weak spot is the approach itself: some sentences get skipped and have to be typed in by hand, the 5-minute cap and portrait mode annoy on iPad, and on songs auto-captions barely work.
apps.loved: Accurate speech recognition even in noise, support for longer clips, simple clear interface, responsive devs on small fixes
apps.weak: Skips some sentences that must be typed in manually, 5-minute cap on free, stuck in portrait on iPad, barely works on songs, thin position and font customization
apps.whoFor: Creators making YouTube and social clips who need auto-captions for regular speech, not music

quotes.text: The auto caption is good, but only when it works. There are a lot of sentences it just skips all together, which I have to then manually add in.
I tried adding captions to my video but they’re always stuck at the very bottom of the screen, how am I able to move the text around?

apps.title: Teleprompter-Record Script
apps.verdict: As a teleprompter it functions, some find it handy, with a landscape mode and even a face-beautify feature. But the model is openly a trap: it lets you shoot the whole video and only then tells you export costs money, there's no trial, and mid-shoot a subscription window interrupts and the recording is lost. Worse, after payment the app demands a Chinese phone number and won't launch without one, so people lose their money.
apps.loved: Working teleprompter, landscape mode, clear text, face beautify
apps.weak: Export is paid and hidden until you finish shooting, no trial, subscription window interrupts shooting and the recording is lost, after payment it demands a Chinese phone number and won't launch
apps.whoFor: Almost no one outside China: without a Chinese phone number the app won't work even after you pay.

apps.title: Teleprompter — Video & Mirror
apps.verdict: A simple teleprompter for speeches, lectures and video: handy speed and font-size control, and it genuinely saves some people on shoots. But the free version is nearly useless, and basic things like pasting text, renaming and saving scripts demand the paid version. Worse, 'bug fix' updates wiped people's entire script libraries and broke saving of edits.
apps.loved: Scroll-speed and font-size control, saves people on speech and lecture shoots, simple interface
apps.weak: Free version nearly useless without paying, can't paste text or rename a script without the paid one, updates deleted the script library, doesn't save edits, no face-on video mode in free
apps.whoFor: People who need a simple scrolling prompter for speeches and video recording and are ready to pay upfront

quotes.text: There should be a line going through the middle of a screen which is where the speaker's eyes should be at all times. If he or she starts reading from the top of the screen, it'll be obvious to the viewer that

apps.title: Teleprompter - VILO
apps.verdict: The idea lands: it's easy to read a script while looking straight into the camera, plus AI script, captions, and green-screen background removal. In practice it often breaks: video hangs on screen forever, won't save or can't be found after recording, screens don't fit the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and green screen and AI filters die in landscape.
apps.loved: Reading a script with eyes on the camera, smooth scrolling, AI script generation, captions, green-screen background removal, video quality stays intact
apps.weak: Video freezes or won't save after recording, screens don't fit newer iPhones, AI filters and green screen fail in landscape, mic records sound only half the time, the promised free trial turns into an instant charge
apps.whoFor: People filming talking-head clips for social and online courses who can tolerate flaky recording

quotes.text: I get very nervous while I am speaking in front of a camera and it does not look natural at all since I can not stop myself looking elsewhere. I was looking for a teleprompter app that could help me remember what to say while I am speaking and helping me keep eye contact wi

apps.title: Captions & Teleprompter AI
apps.verdict: The idea is good, lots of fonts and word highlighting, but people hit the same failures again and again: the export button does nothing even after paying, the app crashes on long videos, and caption edits don't survive reopening the project. Auto captions come out with errors that are hard to fix by hand. Many paid for a subscription and still couldn't get a finished video out at all.
apps.loved: Lots of fonts and colors, word highlighting, the script teleprompter idea, voice-to-text input
apps.weak: Export button doesn't work even after paying, crashes on long videos, caption edits aren't saved, auto captions have errors and are hard to fix, money taken with no usable result
apps.whoFor: Hard to recommend to anyone until export and edit-saving are fixed, too many people are left with no finished video

quotes.text: The captions always had to be fixed so I stopped using it and then when I attempted to use the teleprompter, it doesn’t appear to be accessible.

apps.title: Translate Add Subtitles Video
apps.verdict: The idea is useful: drop in a foreign-language clip and get a translation with captions, and for some it served for years on videos from friends. But translation quality often fails from Italian, Spanish and Bengali, the app freezes and loses hours of work, and even after paying a remaining-minutes counter keeps ticking.
apps.loved: Translating foreign-language clips, auto-captions on video, decent recognition with clear speech, responsive support for some, years of use on friends' videos
apps.weak: Translation often inaccurate from Italian, Spanish and Bengali, freezes losing hours of work, minutes counter keeps ticking even after paying, strips audio from the clip without an upgrade
apps.whoFor: People who receive foreign-language clips and want to quickly understand them with captions in their own language

quotes.text: Submitted a video in Spanish to be transcribed and translated into English and it did a very poor job of translating. I’d like a refund for my subscription

apps.title: Caption Expert
apps.verdict: People come for ready-made post captions when they're out of ideas, and for some this bank genuinely helps and even grows their follower count. But many are put off by the content itself: captions get called childish and same-y, saving to favorites is locked behind a subscription, saving flat-out fails, and 10 dollars a week feels absurd.
apps.loved: Big bank of ready-made post captions, option to write your own, helps quickly find text for a photo, easy to use
apps.weak: Captions called childish and repetitive, saving flat-out fails, favorites locked behind a subscription, support unreachable during the trial, 10 dollars a week pricing
apps.whoFor: Teens and social creators who want a quick caption bank for posts without writing their own

apps.title: Subtitles: Captions For Video
apps.verdict: When it works, creators like the speech recognition and font choices for captions. But there's almost no stability: uploads hang at 99% with a PrimaryAPIError, the app crashes on word-by-word animations, projects won't reopen, and captions come out without a single comma or capital letter, unusable for real work.
apps.loved: Decent speech recognition, rich font choice, captions burned into the clip, fast when it works
apps.weak: Uploads hang at 99% with an error, crashes on word-by-word animations, projects won't reopen, captions with no commas or capitals, captions out of sync with audio
apps.whoFor: People who want stylish captions on short clips and can tolerate frequent failures

quotes.text: when you are editing a caption and try to move it to the correct place- it gets stuck on other captions sometimes in the middle of another caption and you cant unstick it!

apps.title: Captions AI for Videos - Dubs
apps.verdict: People come for AI dubbing and subtitles, and some praise how well it catches the voice. But most hit a wall: you pay a subscription, then still have to buy credits and seconds to finish your own video, and the money gets charged while the seconds never show up. The watermark also lands right in the middle of the frame instead of the corner.
apps.loved: Voice recognition and dubbing into other languages, support with a month-long guarantee, easy to start
apps.weak: Must buy extra credits and seconds on top of the subscription, money charged but seconds not added, watermark right in the center of the video, slow processing, hard to cancel the subscription
apps.whoFor: People making short voiced videos with subtitles who are willing to deal with paying extra for seconds

apps.title: ▶Teleprompter
apps.verdict: A simple teleprompter that works for some people for singing with a band, training videos and rehearsals, with pleasant speech-paced scrolling. But the headline feature breaks: after paying for gold, voice scroll doesn't actually listen to your words, it just moves on any noise or music. Plus a basic pain, you can't save the scroll speed you want, it resets to a too-fast value every time you open a script, and there's no support or a real website.
apps.loved: Smooth speech-paced scrolling, handy for singing with a band and training videos, simple and clear
apps.weak: Voice scroll moves on any noise not your words even after paying for gold, can't save scroll speed and it resets to too fast, no support or real website, broken settings on iPad, can't change font size or color
apps.whoFor: People who need a dead-simple prompter for singing or rehearsals and don't care about voice scroll

quotes.text: The auto scroll is suppose to move as you speak....sure does...if music plays (with no one is singing), when other people speak in the background
The fatal flaw is the inability to save a desired scroll speed. Every time you open a script it reverts back to the default 50, which is way too fast.
the Scroll up and down functions on a presentation remote (like podcaster) no longer works with this app. So I bit the bullet and got another teleprompter app for $90/year.
So many times after recording a several minute video, I click the camera to save it, and my recording disappears. That’s very frustrating.

scenarios.name: Solo creators shooting short videos for social
scenarios.job: Record a clip for TikTok, Reels or YouTube in one take, looking into the camera without stumbling, then lay on large captions so the video gets watched without sound
scenarios.gap: Authors discuss unexpected charges for export and running short of credits. An estimate of the result available for the chosen clip, made in advance, would help.

scenarios.name: Speakers before a one-off important appearance
scenarios.job: Read a speech at a funeral, wedding, thesis defense, lecture or campaign clip so the teleprompter itself matches the live pace of speech and it does not show that you are reading
scenarios.gap: Authors describe a limit on duration and paid voice tracking. Before the event they have to be able to test the mode they need and the whole script.

scenarios.name: Production pros and regular presenters
scenarios.job: Build a teleprompter into the workflow on an ongoing basis: mirroring for a hardware rig, remote control, sync between iPad and iPhone, stable recording without glitches on a shoot or on stage
scenarios.gap: Authors ask for a saved speed and stable syncing. A separate run-through of the script after the text or the device changes would help.

scenarios.name: People who need accurate captions and translation
scenarios.job: Automatically get clean subtitles under a video, including for the deaf and hard of hearing, or to translate someone else’s clip into their language with minimal manual fixing
scenarios.gap: The reviews describe phrases that were skipped and errors in the direction of writing. The source language, the timing and the final export need checking, especially for accessibility captions.
